# Set-up

This markdown will generate `CellBender` appropriate input files. `CellBender` traditionally takes the raw `h5` file produced by cellranger as input and performs both cell-calling as well as ambient removal. For the engineered datasets, we will need to generate equivalent files containing the cells (generated [here](Tonsils_10xFlex_make_engineered_datasets.html)) as well as empty cells (generated [here](Tonsils_10xFlex_make_engineered_emptyObject.html)). 

`CellBender` performs a lot better when provided with the input parameters `expected-cells` and `total-droplets-included`. We can estimate both of these input parameters from the resulting knee plot. In our case, we actually know the number of expected cells is going to be 12,000


## Load libraries

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(here)
  library(glue)
  library(DropletUtils)
  library(scran)
  library(scater)
  library(scuttle)
  library(scales)
  library(readr)
  library(Seurat)
  library(scDblFinder)
  library(scMerge)
  library(ggpubr)
  library(BiocParallel)
  library(clustree)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scMerge)
  library(Matrix)
  library(SeuratDisk)
  library(qs2)
  library(patchwork)
})


```

## Load data


```{r}
#load empty cells
sce_empty <- read10xCounts(here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Engineered/Tonsils_10xFlex_engineered_emptyObject"), 
                           row.names = "symbol", col.names = T)

#list of paths to all engineered datasets
list_datasets_paths <- list.dirs(path = here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Engineered/"), full.names = T)
list_datasets_paths <- list_datasets_paths[grepl("Tonsils_10xFlex_engineered_12k_0.15p",list_datasets_paths)]

list_datasets <- lapply(list_datasets_paths, function(path) read10xCounts(path,row.names = "symbol", col.names = T))

names(list_datasets) <- basename(list_datasets_paths)
```

# Combine empty cells + engineered to generate `h5` file output

Write a function to do this. 

```{r}

run_combine_export <- function(cells, 
                               empties,
                               name){
  #make sure genes match
  gene_universe <- intersect(rownames(cells), rownames(empties))
  cells <- cells[gene_universe,]
  empties <- empties[ gene_universe,]
  #check order 
  stopifnot(all(rownames(cells) == rownames(empties)))
  
  #combine
  combined <- cbind(counts(cells),counts(empties))
  
  #export
  filename <- sprintf("%s/%s_cellbenderInput_feature_bc_matrix.h5", unique(dirname(list_datasets_paths)), name)
  write10xCounts(path = filename,
               x = combined,
               type = "HDF5",
               version = "3",
               barcodes = colnames(combined),
               gene.symbol = rownames(combined), 
               overwrite = TRUE)
  print(filename)
  return(combined) #keep file name
}

```

Run for all engineered datasets

```{r, warning=FALSE}

list_out <- sapply(1:length(list_datasets), function(IN){
  run_combine_export(cells = list_datasets[[IN]],
                     empties = sce_empty, 
                     name = names(list_datasets)[IN])
})


names(list_out) <-basename(list_datasets_paths)
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
#silent clean up
rm(list_datasets, sce_empty, list_datasets_paths);gc()

```


# Make Kneeplots for engineered datasets

For each of the engineered 'raw' files, let's make a kneeplot and highlight potential thresholds for `-total-droplet-included`. The `-total-droplet-included` does not have to be exact- every droplet/barcode past that threshold will however be treated as an empty droplet. 

Make a function

```{r}
run_kneeplot <- function(counts, 
                         label_df, 
                         name){
  bcrank <- barcodeRanks(counts) #using DropletUtils function
  bcrank_filtered <- bcrank[!duplicated(bcrank$rank), ]# only show unique points for plotting speed
  
  ggplot(data = bcrank_filtered, aes(x = log10(rank), log10(total))) + geom_point()+
    geom_vline(data= label_df, mapping = aes(xintercept = log10(num), colour = name)) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unname(Polychrome::alphabet.colors(nrow(label_df))))+
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), legend.text = element_text(size=15), 
                       legend.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "cm"), legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "cm"))+
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 2)))+
    ggtitle(sprintf('Knee plot:\n%s', name))
  
}

```


```{r, warning=FALSE}
#set same test thresholds for all
label_df <- data.frame(name=c("cells_12k", "droplet_45k"),
                       num = c(12000, 45000))

plot_list <- sapply(1:length(list_out), function(IN){
  run_kneeplot(counts = list_out[[IN]], label_df = label_df, name=names(list_out)[IN])
})
```

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.height=8, fig.width=15}
wrap_plots(plot_list, guides = "collect", axes = "collect") 
```

We can use the same thresholds for all engineered datasets.
